Solve the programming problem carefully and submit only a verified solution.

1. Parse the statement and constraints precisely. Identify the required API/entrypoint, input/output format, indexing, and edge cases. Restate the key condition in your own words before coding.
2. Derive an algorithm whose worst-case time and memory fit the constraints (not merely the samples). Be especially suspicious of hidden quadratic work, repeated preprocessing, recursion depth, integer overflow, and language/runtime constants.
3. Implement a complete, simple program in the required language/API. Keep the final submitted code self-contained and ensure it handles the exact judge interface.
4. Run `run_tests` on the submitted candidate. Treat every failed example as a hard blocker: diagnose the specific mismatch, revise the algorithm/code, and run the full tests again. Never submit a candidate with even one public example failing, and do not assume an example is optional because another one passes.
5. Before submission, perform a compact adversarial review. Check minimum/maximum sizes, empty or singleton cases, duplicates/ties, all-equal and strictly ordered data, boundary indices, disconnected/degenerate structures, and numerical limits as applicable.
